recommendationReason: Walkz has reached Milestone 7 with its evidence-first review, proof, hosted, and approved-fix paths intact. Continue toward a reproducible single-host beta while keeping real-user outcome validation as a separate gate.

project.name: Walkz
project.problem: Pull-request reviewers can produce plausible findings without evidence that a change caused a real regression.
project.user: Solo developers and small-team maintainers who need evidence before merging a pull request.
project.outcome: A maintainer can run Walkz locally or through its GitHub App and receive an evidence-bound verdict, approve a verified fix, and operate the hosted stack from one reproducible release.
project.deliverySurface: Cross-platform CLI plus a self-hosted GitHub App, worker, and dashboard
triggeredOverlays: Schema, protocol, public API or migration
project.overlayDecision: Private source may cross a provider boundary, BYOK and GitHub credentials require protection, and repository code may execute inside proof containers. The hosted stack adds durable migrations, asynchronous workers, a dashboard, and distributed release images, so service, contract, interface, and artifact checks all apply.

repositorySearch.capability: Bounded Git patch parsing, changed-line indexing, shell-free cross-platform command execution, descendant termination, evidence policy, and structured AI review.
repositorySearch.summary: Five credible repositories were checked. Adopt jsdiff and Execa behind Walkz-owned boundaries, inspect reviewdog and ReviewGate for tests and policy patterns, and reject Qodo PR-Agent as an architectural dependency. No repository supplies Walkz's evidence engine or base/head proof.

claims.text: CodeRabbit already provides most of the visible Milestone 1 local review workflow, so Walkz's defensible difference begins with counterfactual proof.
Model review can miss defects, invent findings, and propose unsafe fixes, so model output cannot control the final verdict.
Synthetic broken and clean fixtures prove engineering behavior but do not establish usefulness on real pull requests.
Shell-free process execution can limit injection, but Milestone 1 commands still run with developer authority and descendant termination is best-effort.
A local Groq review still sends selected private source off the machine and may face temporary provider retention unless ZDR is enabled.
Active model IDs, structured-output support, free limits, and provider failures are separate mutable facts that must be checked and recorded.
Git metadata and external diff helpers can execute code, while unusual paths require literal and NUL-delimited handling.
jsdiff v9 and Execa v10 cover two failure-prone boundaries behind replaceable adapters; neither supplies Walkz's evidence semantics.

A proof plan cannot authorize its own command. The exact command digest must appear in an approval set supplied outside the plan, and every proof byte and resource limit is bound to a stable plan digest.
Walkz can reconstruct exact base and head trees from Git objects without changing the developer's checkout, applying checkout filters, or leaving proof data behind.
Walkz can run the same approved proof against exact base and head trees in non-root containers with no runtime network or host secrets, bounded resources, and verified cleanup.
Walkz can measure two golden proof fixtures, including catch rate, false positives, proof rate, proof duration, and model metadata, without treating synthetic results as product evidence.

Walkz has a standalone production Compose contract that binds API, web, and worker services to one clean source revision, isolates durable data, exposes only the web edge, and runs application processes with reduced authority.
Walkz exposes bounded API, worker, queue, outbox, latency, and failure telemetry without repository identifiers, source, prompts, responses, credentials, job IDs, or raw errors.

Walkz can restore a known review from a bounded logical backup, rebuild disposable review queue state from PostgreSQL, run a newer exact application revision, and roll back to an older exact revision without retaining the synthetic backup or drill resources.

sources.title: CodeRabbit Command-Line Review Tool
sources.decisionImpact: Shows that local Git scopes, diagnostics, terminal output, and structured findings are existing table stakes.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot Agents responsible-use guidance
sources.decisionImpact: Supports human review, testing, and a deterministic boundary because AI review can miss issues or invent them.

sources.title: Is Agentic Code Review Helpful?
sources.decisionImpact: Its observed rejection rate makes precision and dismissal cost better outcome measures than finding count.

sources.title: Bigger Isn't Always Better: A Comparative Evaluation of LLMs for Automated Code Review
sources.decisionImpact: Shows that synthetic fixtures are engineering checks, not enough evidence of usefulness on real pull requests.

sources.title: Node.js 24 child process documentation
sources.decisionImpact: Defines shell-free argument execution, Windows command limitations, cancellation, and incomplete descendant termination.

sources.title: Node.js DEP0190 shell argument deprecation
sources.decisionImpact: Rules out passing configured arguments through shell-enabled spawn or execFile.

sources.title: Git security guidance
sources.decisionImpact: Narrows Milestone 1 to developer-trusted Git metadata and forbids bypassing Git ownership protection.

sources.title: Git diff format
sources.decisionImpact: Requires NUL-delimited machine records and explicit handling of unusual and quoted paths.

sources.title: Groq Structured Outputs
sources.decisionImpact: Supports schema-constrained responses on selected models while still requiring local semantic validation.

sources.title: Your Data in GroqCloud
sources.decisionImpact: Requires a private-code disclosure because inference data can be retained for reliability or abuse review unless ZDR is enabled.

sources.title: Groq Supported Models
sources.decisionImpact: Supports setup-time discovery but not blind selection of the first active model.

sources.title: Groq Rate Limits
sources.decisionImpact: Requires account-aware budgets, Retry-After handling, and an inconclusive result when bounded retries are exhausted.

sources.title: Groq API Error Codes and Responses
sources.decisionImpact: Defines the provider failure classes that need separate retry and verdict behavior.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218A
sources.decisionImpact: Supports treating model inputs, outputs, versions, tests, and human oversight as lifecycle risks for an AI system.

sources.title: jsdiff v9 Git patch parser
sources.decisionImpact: Supplies strict hunk validation and Git path parsing behind a small, replaceable Walkz wrapper.

sources.title: Execa v10 termination documentation
sources.decisionImpact: Provides maintained cross-platform descendant termination while documenting its best-effort limits.

sources.title: Git attributes documentation
sources.decisionImpact: Shows that checkout can apply attribute-driven conversions and smudge filters, which proof materialization must avoid.

sources.title: Git cat-file documentation
sources.decisionImpact: Defines the batch protocol used to read exact object bytes through one bounded Git process.

sources.title: Docker container run reference
sources.decisionImpact: Defines read-only filesystems, pull policy, numeric users, capability removal, process limits, security options, tmpfs mounts, entrypoint overrides, and other runtime flags.

sources.title: Docker none network driver
sources.decisionImpact: Confirms that the none driver creates only the loopback device inside the proof container.

sources.title: Docker container resource constraints
sources.decisionImpact: Defines CPU and memory limits and confirms that equal memory and memory-swap values disable container swap.

sources.title: Docker logging configuration
sources.decisionImpact: Documents that the default json-file driver can exhaust disk and that the none driver prevents daemon-side log retention.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 pg_dump documentation
sources.decisionImpact: Supports a consistent custom-format logical dump that is compressed and can be inspected before restore.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 pg_restore documentation
sources.decisionImpact: Supports fail-fast restoration of the custom archive into a fresh isolated database.

sources.title: Docker Compose up reference
sources.decisionImpact: Supports health-gated startup for services in the uniquely scoped drill project.

sources.title: Docker Compose down reference
sources.decisionImpact: Supports explicit removal of the drill project's named volumes during cleanup.

assumptions.text: Counterfactual evidence will help maintainers make better or faster merge decisions than existing local review workflows.
assumptions.impact: This is the product thesis and cannot be proven by Milestone 1 fixtures.
assumptions.nextCheck: After Milestone 2, compare Walkz with CodeRabbit or checks plus an assistant on 10 to 20 historical real defects.

assumptions.text: Execa can execute approved commands without shell interpolation and terminate the tested descendant trees on Windows and Linux.
assumptions.impact: A failure blocks the runner contract and may require a narrower command policy.
assumptions.nextCheck: Repeat the process-tree and secret tests whenever the execution adapter or supported platform set changes.

assumptions.text: At least one free Groq production model can return useful schema-valid reviews within the configured token and latency budgets.
assumptions.impact: Without it, the model path remains inconclusive and Walkz narrows to deterministic checks.
assumptions.nextCheck: Probe capabilities during doctor and score the selected model on the golden fixtures before accepting the provider phase.

contradictions.text: Milestone 1 requires a broken fixture to return FIX, while default policy permits only VERIFIED findings to block and proof begins in Milestone 2.
contradictions.resolution: The broken fixture explicitly opts into blocking SUPPORTED deterministic evidence. Default repositories still block only VERIFIED evidence, and UNVERIFIED model findings never block.

contradictions.text: Earlier research deferred Execa pending a standard-library spike, while Execa v10 now implements the required cross-platform descendant behavior.
contradictions.resolution: Adopt Execa behind Walkz interfaces, retain direct process-tree tests, and keep its best-effort limitation visible.

contradictions.text: Existing tools cover most Milestone 1 features, which weakens the case for another standalone local reviewer.
contradictions.resolution: Treat Milestone 1 as a time-boxed foundation. Continue only toward the base/head proof that existing finalists did not demonstrate.

decisions.text: Build Milestone 1 as the bounded local foundation for counterfactual proof, then reassess differentiation with real evidence.
The model proposes findings only. Deterministic code validates locations, coverage, evidence levels, and the final verdict.
Use jsdiff parsePatch and Execa behind Walkz-owned adapters; keep evidence, policy, path containment, approval, and provider logic local.
Make the safe runner the first implementation slice because command execution, secret inheritance, and process cleanup carry the highest immediate cost.
Disclose private-code transfer before first model use, keep no-model useful, select a compatible free production model explicitly, and return INCONCLUSIVE when provider evidence is insufficient.
Keep command approval outside the proof plan. Bind the approved command, exact revisions, reproducer bytes, pinned image, isolation settings, and limits into one stable digest before execution.
Build proof workspaces from bounded Git tree and object reads instead of checkout operations, then reject unsupported entries and remove every temporary workspace.

Prepare a digest-pinned image without host credentials, then run the approved command with no pull or network, reduced authority, bounded resources, direct output capture, and verified container cleanup.

gates.trigger: All six Milestone 1 phases and their focused reviews pass.
gates.requiredEvidence: Clean npm ci, build, unit and integration suites, provider error matrix, CLI fixture verdicts, Windows paths with spaces, and a 60-second local demo tied to one commit.

gates.trigger: Proof contracts, authorization, hashing, and budget allocation are implemented.
gates.requiredEvidence: Focused boundary tests, a red authorization mutation, workspace typecheck, full and shuffled suites, and available security scans.

gates.trigger: Exact base and head proof workspaces are implemented.
gates.requiredEvidence: Dirty-tree preservation, exact SHA binding, path and link rejection, unusual-name coverage, paths with spaces, cancellation, and cleanup tests.

gates.trigger: Locked container execution is implemented for proof plans.
gates.requiredEvidence: Self-contained proof files run against base and head after separate credential-free image preparation, with the same pinned image and approved command, no runtime network or inherited secrets, bounded CPU, memory, disk, output and process count, timeout handling, and cleanup. Repository package installation remains unsupported and cannot run implicitly.

gates.trigger: Paired proof outcomes are classified and attached to findings.
gates.requiredEvidence: Only base-pass and head-fail outcomes create VERIFIED evidence. Exact plan, command, image, revision, sanitized output, and artifact hashes remain bound, while timeout, cancellation, infrastructure failure, truncation, or cleanup failure stay inconclusive.
One identical reproducer passes on base, fails on head, creates VERIFIED evidence, cleans its data, and passes from a clean clone on Windows and Ubuntu.

gates.trigger: The standalone production Compose deployment is implemented.
gates.requiredEvidence: Exact clean-revision images, no production builds or bind mounts, web-only host publishing, internal durable data services, fail-fast configuration, reduced application privileges, health checks, migrations, and disposable live-stack cleanup.

gates.trigger: Phase 7.3 adds bounded operational telemetry without private review content.
gates.requiredEvidence: Health, queue, worker, outbox, latency, and failure signals are useful for operation, bounded in cardinality, free of source code and credentials, and covered by focused and full tests.

gates.trigger: Phase 7.4 rehearses backup, restore, queued-work recovery, upgrade, and rollback.
gates.requiredEvidence: A bounded synthetic backup restores a known review and migration ledger, PostgreSQL reconstructs missing Redis work, exact candidate and baseline images run in order, and cleanup removes the backup and all drill resources.

gates.trigger: Milestone 2 counterfactual proof exists and 10 to 20 historical real defects are available.
